cells.value: Exact capability table from the October 9 report. These are recorded implementation and proof claims, not newly executed tests.
List/read/create/write/replace/JSON edit/copy/move/delete; durable preimages, mode preservation, history, readback, restore
Configured mounts and operator-owned ancestors matter; unrelated external writers are not coordinated automatically
Typed, operator-defined argv recipes; bounded output, timeout cleanup, recorded exit status
The process runs with host permissions; this is not arbitrary untrusted-code isolation
Dynamic capability registry; profiles narrow capabilities, roots, accounts, effects, recipes
Broad catalog availability is not evidence every provider operation is configured or authorized
Discovery, exact skill selection, content digest verification, tool/schema validation, named-account execution
Each actual target must supply its own working configuration and identity
Installed 1.5.1 completed real skill search/load, tool search, and schema lookup; exact destination restriction active
Execution stopped before Mem0; this particular live check proves preflight compatibility only
One full live cycle on Javar's isolated canary, including rejection checks, separate readback, and restoration
This was an owned scratch file; receipt explicitly says running-agent activation was not demonstrated; Javante was not proven
Sourced bindings and narrow-only profile selection; local allowed/denied tests
Runtime use of those accounts by both agents remains unproven; the Orgo account label in the canary receipt was caller asserted
SQLite intent before effects, stable operation IDs, persisted manifests/receipts, resume/replay, process locking
Same-ledger locking does not establish distributed fleet ownership or coordination across separate ledgers
Scoped bounded recall; one live retrieval on installed 1.5.0 returned one memory
No live worker-delivery, relevance-quality, automatic-capture, or two-agent recall proof follows from that single retrieval
Exact recall-block hash and size/item bounds; default behavior keeps recall with the caller unless delivery is approved
A caller-side receipt is not proof a worker received the memory; 1.5.1 did not alter these approval paths
Configured publisher, original-content backup, revision checks, separate readback, conflict-aware restore; local tests
Live isolated destination and registered Drive write/readback route were unresolved in the inspected evidence
Typed choice/score interfaces, abstention, schema validation, provenance/error handling; local tests
Named account/skill/model and live inference/quality evidence remain unresolved; no sales policy is supplied by these types
Codex dispatch, repair, knowledge maintenance, memory primitives, and Bridge/Observatory interfaces retained
Reuse and inspect these before treating historical fleet concerns as missing code
Separate local Codex SessionStart/failure/Stop activation passed its native acceptance
Separate subsystem; it does not prove Hermes hook installation or fleet event subscriptions
